lines.text: In the Valley of Peace lives Le Chonk. He is round. He is orange. He is... a kung fu cat.
Wolf bandits ran through the village. Papa Canard needs help. So Le Chonk smashes crates... and eats the dumplings.
Master Tortue sends him to find five Jade Stones. One in a tree. One on an island. One in a cracked boulder: only a belly can break it. One in the wolf camp.
Then comes Overfit, the tiger. He learned every kung fu move in the world. Punch? Predicted!
So Le Chonk eats the Dragon Noodles, and becomes Dragon Chonk. One Dragon Belly... that was not in the training data!
But who plays Le Chonk? Mistral Large Four. Every turn, it reads a short text: the quest, its health, the things nearby. About three hundred tokens. No images.
Then it picks one action, like go, talk, hit or fight, on a target. The game does the walking and the aiming. While Mistral thinks, the world waits.
These are its real thoughts. And the game is deterministic, so every run replays exactly.
Three runs. Three wins. About five minutes of game time, fifty turns, and four to five cents per run.
Press Let Chonk play, and watch the master. Or play it yourself. The link is below.
